issues.legal_issue: An appeal by a reconstituted partnership remains competent when the partnership that contracted with the opposing party has not been dissolved and the appeal is brought by a partner connected to that partnership.
material_facts: The contracting firm had been reconstituted several times, and there was no allegation that it had been dissolved.
A partner who represented the firm in the High Court had been a partner in the contracting firm and was a party to the agreement.
A second firm with the same name had been registered, but the court treated that registration as a mistake that did not alter the status of the contracting firm.
issues.conclusion: The objection that the appeal was not brought by the contracting firm was unsustainable.
issues.legal_principle: The court treated the continuing partnership, rather than the later duplicate registration, as the relevant contracting firm: reconstitution did not establish dissolution, and a partner of the continuing firm could represent it in the appeal.

predicates.appeal_concerning_partnership_contract: The proceeding is an appeal concerning a contract made by a partnership.
predicates.firm_not_dissolved: The partnership that made the contract has not been dissolved.
predicates.appeal_representative_connected_to_contr: The person representing the partnership in the appeal was a partner in the contracting firm and was connected to the contract.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns a partnership contract, the firm has not been dissolved, and its representative is connected to the contracting firm, the appeal is competent as an appeal by that firm.

issues.legal_issue: Interim protection pending arbitration cannot be granted merely on the basis of a claimed right to continue a fixed-term commercial arrangement when the right to enforce that arrangement is uncertain and the grounds for appellate interference are inadequate.
material_facts: The company sought interim relief to continue mining operations after the latest extension of its raising contract had expired.
The company argued that the arrangement continued with the mining leases and relied on its investments and machinery.
The partnership disputed that claim, maintained that the agreement had been for a fixed term, and stated that it intended to conduct mining itself.

The High Court had set aside the District Court's status quo order, and the Supreme Court considered the asserted right to specifically enforce the agreement insufficiently clear at the interlocutory stage.
The Supreme Court left the underlying contractual rights and the final applicability of the Specific Relief Act for the arbitral tribunal or an appropriate case.
issues.conclusion: The company had not shown adequate grounds for the Supreme Court to interfere with the High Court's refusal of interim relief; the appeal was dismissed. The court did not finally decide whether the Specific Relief Act controls the exercise of interim powers pending arbitration.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 9 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, an ordinary court's consideration of interim relief is, prima facie, governed by recognized principles for interim injunctions and other interim protection. The court indicated that the Act did not prima facie exclude the Specific Relief Act, but expressly left the question open. It distinguished Firm Ashok Traders v. Gurumukh Das Saluja, (2004) 3 SCC 155, as not finally answering that question. Sections 14 and 41 of the Specific Relief Act were relied on by the respondent, but their application to this agreement was not decided. The underlying questions about the contract's duration and specific enforceability were left to the arbitrator.

predicates.appeal_from_refusal_of_interim_protectio: The proceeding is an appeal from a refusal of interim protection sought while a dispute is to be resolved by arbitration.
predicates.claimed_right_to_continue_contract_is_un: The party seeking interim protection claims a right to continue a commercial arrangement, but the record does not clearly establish that right at the interim stage.
predicates.grounds_for_appellate_interference_are_i: The party seeking appellate relief has not shown adequate grounds to overturn the lower court's refusal of interim protection.

issues.definition: In an appeal about interim protection pending arbitration, if the claimed right to continue a contract is uncertain and the grounds for appellate intervention are inadequate, the refusal of interim protection is left undisturbed.

issues.legal_issue: A court may appoint a sole arbitrator to resolve the parties' disputes when the agreed arbitral tribunal has not been constituted and the parties agree to the court making the appointment.
material_facts: The parties had each nominated an arbitrator under their agreement, but those arbitrators had not nominated a presiding arbitrator despite the passage of more than a year.
The application seeking appointment of a third arbitrator was pending, and the parties agreed that the Supreme Court could appoint either a presiding arbitrator or a sole arbitrator.
The Supreme Court appointed a former Chief Justice of India as sole arbitrator to decide disputes arising from the parties' agreement and power of attorney.
issues.conclusion: The court appointed a sole arbitrator to decide the parties' disputes and revoked the parties' earlier nominations of arbitrators.
issues.legal_principle: The court acted after the agreed appointment procedure had failed to constitute the tribunal and both parties agreed that the court could appoint a sole or presiding arbitrator. The appointment was made in the context of the parties' arbitration agreement and the pending request for appointment under Section 11(4)(b) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996.

predicates.arbitration_dispute: The parties have a dispute that they agreed to resolve by arbitration.
predicates.agreed_tribunal_not_constituted: The parties' agreed appointment procedure has failed to constitute the arbitral tribunal.
predicates.parties_agree_to_court_appointment: Both parties agree that the court may appoint an arbitrator to resolve the dispute.

issues.definition: When an arbitration dispute exists, the agreed tribunal has not been constituted, and both parties agree to court appointment, the court appoints a sole arbitrator.
